deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German notes on ancient history, almost certainly lecture or reading notes, covering the Seleucid kingdom from the end of Antiochus II Theos to Seleucus II Callinicus. It continues directly from fol. 159 (Antiochus II, his wife Laodice, his sister Apame, and the war with Ptolemy II Philadelphus) and runs on to fol. 161 (death of Seleucus II, then Seleucus III and Antiochus III).

The content, paragraph by paragraph:

(1) The war with Ptolemy Philadelphus 'was conducted with great vehemence' ('Er wurde mit großer Heftigkeit geführt'). This is the Second Syrian War. It ended with Antiochus II repudiating Laodice and marrying Berenice, Ptolemy's daughter. Laodice was not content with this, so Antiochus took Laodice back.

(2) Under Antiochus II a 'revolution' occurred in inner Asia. The Bactrian and Parthian realms broke away around 250 BC, and this 'laid the foundation stone for the decline of the empire.' Margin: '247 † durch Gift', i.e. Antiochus died in 247, by poison.

(3) His son Seleucus II Callinicus followed, reigning 247–227 according to the notes. The hatred between Laodice and Berenice broke out anew. Margin: 'Berenice umgebracht' (Berenice murdered).

(4) This led to a new war with Egypt, the Third Syrian or Laodicean War. The Egyptian king came with a large fleet and army and seized Syria and Cilicia. Seleucus suffered with his fleet (reading uncertain) but eventually recovered his states.

(5) Seleucus was then drawn into a new war, 243–240, with his brother Antiochus Hierax, governor of (Asia Minor). The name 'Antiochus' is supplied by an insertion mark '†' and the marginal note '† Antiochus'. A second margin note reads 'Seleucus siegte' (Seleucus won).

(6) He held the throne because the Egyptian king had to undertake other great expeditions.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations. The handwriting is a rounded cursive and does not resemble Gauss's hand. The notes are probably a student or lecture notebook bound into the bundle, possibly from history lectures at Göttingen such as Heeren's; this is unsure.
errors: Historical dating is off by about one year by modern chronology. Antiochus II reigned c. 261–246 BC, not 262–247, and died in 246, not 247. Seleucus II reigned 246–225 BC, not 247–227.

The margin note 'Seleucus siegte' contradicts the standard account. In the War of the Brothers, Seleucus II was decisively defeated by Antiochus Hierax (with Galatian mercenaries) at Ancyra, c. 240/239 BC. The war is usually dated c. 241/240–237 or later, not 243–240.

The secession of Bactria and Parthia (c. 250–245 BC, Diodotus and Andragoras/Arsaces) is placed under Antiochus II. That is acceptable but chronologically disputed. The digit read by the machine as '150' must be 250 (BC).
The poisoning of Antiochus II by Laodice is ancient tradition (e.g. Appian, Justin), not established fact. The notes present it as fact, which is normal for period lecture notes.
Seleucus's fleet was, according to Justin, destroyed by a storm. The text's wording here is uncertain ('behielt nur'/'verlor'?), so it may or may not reflect this.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'mit großer Herrlichkeit[?] geehrt[?]' should read 'mit großer Heftigkeit geführt'. The subject 'Er' is the war (Krieg) from the previous page, which then 'endigte sich damit'.
'rissen sich 150[?] los' should read 'rissen sich 250 los' (c. 250 BC).
'Partische' is the writer's spelling of 'Parthische'; keep it as written.

'Seleucus verliert[?] seine Flotte' is uncertain. The image looks more like 'Seleucus behielt nur seine Flotte' (or possibly 'verlor seine Flotte'), followed by 'bemächtigte sich aber doch endlich seiner Staaten wieder'.

'seinem Bruder Statthalter von Asien {+†+} Hierax' should read 'seinem Bruder, Statthalter von Asien, † Hierax'. The '†' is an insertion mark keyed to the margin '† Antiochus', giving 'Antiochus Hierax'.

Last line: 'große Expeditionen[?] {+unter+}[?] machte[?]' should read something like 'große Expeditionen unternehmen mußte' (abbreviated 'Expo'; the word 'mußte' carries a superscript insertion mark).
